correctness.rationale: Read the complete assigned RESULT and decisive sections of Ambrus--Gárgyán arXiv:2609.12714v2. The one-positive factorization is exact: if p_j=-a_j/a_1, sum p=1 and Q=sum p_j^2, then a_1=(1+Q)^(-1/2) and exponential convolution gives f(0)=sqrt(1+Q)/product(1+p_j). Its normalization by the facet-parallel p_j=1/(n-1) yields (1), while the dot product with a_* gives cos(theta)=sqrt((1+1/(n-1))/(1+Q)); AM-GM proves (2)-(5) with the correct inequality direction. For a normal with m nonzero coordinates, the source's induction formula gives precisely B_{n,m}; for two-value multiplicities k,n-k, its equation (3.1) or gamma convolution gives R_{n,k} exactly. Source Theorem 2 and Proposition 4 rule out an interior three-value chamber minimum, so the closure-minimum argument yields the explicit rho_n threshold; the source's strict equality classification gives rho_n>1. Independent direct arithmetic produced rho_n for n=3..10 as 1.29903811, 1.02640048, 1.03337849, 1.03621514, 1.02776006, 1.02032919, 1.01553820, 1.01226624, all >1. On a unit tangent geodesic, differentiating the displayed log-density gives first derivative zero and second derivative -(n-2)+(n-1)+(n-1)/n=(2n-1)/n; hence both Hessian formulas and Taylor coefficient follow. The result carefully limits the global distance estimate to 1+epsilon<rho_n and makes no optimality claim.
